content.content:
1	# Document Room
2	
3	A local file metadata index. Python 3.10+ and the standard library are sufficient.
4	
5	Run `python3 document_room.py add policy.md --tag legal --tag policy` from this directory to index the sample policy. Add the second sample with `python3 document_room.py add meeting.txt --tag operations`. `python3 document_room.py search --tag legal --text policy` returns matching metadata as JSON. Multiple tags are combined with AND; tags are trimmed and lowercase, and text matches the relative path without case sensitivity.
6	
7	The default document root is `samples`; metadata is persisted in `.state/documents.json`. Override these with `--root` and `--index` before the subcommand. Re-adding a file refreshes its size, SHA-256 and tags. Search reads the stored metadata, not live file contents. Files must resolve inside the document root. This version does not copy documents, extract content or watch filesystem changes. Use the Python `DocumentRoom.add` and `DocumentRoom.search` methods for the same operations. CLI errors return JSON and exit 2.
8	
9	## Document archiving
10	
11	`python3 document_room.py archive meeting.txt` flips a registered document into the archived state without touching its file, and `DocumentRoom.set_archived(relative_path, archived)` does the same from Python; pass `--restore` (or `archived=False`) to mark it active again. The positional path matches the index's relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `refs`: it is never resolved against the filesystem, the file is not parsed, and archiving or restoring works even when the original file has been deleted. The state is stored as a boolean `archived` field on the record; records written before this feature simply lack the field and are treated as active, without the field being added. Restoring stores `archived: false` explicitly. Setting the same state twice returns the identical record, and no other metadata or references change. The updated full record is printed as JSON with exit 0.
12	
13	The first `add` of a path never stores an `archived` field; re-adding a path that already has the field keeps its archived state along with its references. `search` and `export` (CLI flag `--archive-state`, Python argument `archive_state`) accept only `all`, `active` and `archived`; the default `all` keeps the previous selection unchanged. `active` selects records without a true `archived` field and `archived` only records with `archived: true`, in conjunction with the existing tag and path-text filters. Search still returns the complete stored records sorted by path without filling in a default field; export keeps the same document fields, five file statuses and `complete` rule.
14	
15	With reference expansion (`export --with-references`), the archive filter only chooses the starting documents: every referenced document is pulled in recursively regardless of its archive state, each path still appears once and cycles still terminate. For example, an active `policy.md` that references an archived `meeting.txt` still produces a manifest containing both under `--archive-state active --with-references`.
16	
17	Archiving only modifies the index; searching only reads stored metadata; exporting keeps its live file checks and never writes a manifest. Setting the archive state, or filtering with a state other than `all`, validates the whole index: invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures, references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths, and a non-boolean `archived` field all raise `ValueError`, even when the bad record is not selected. A non-string or unregistered path, a non-boolean `archived`, or a non-string/illegal `archive_state` also raises `ValueError`; index read/write failures raise `OSError`, and failed input validation never changes the index. With no index, setting the state is treated as an unregistered path and creates no file, while filtering returns an empty result (an empty manifest has `complete` false). The CLI prints JSON and exits 0 on success, or a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures.
18	
19	## Document categories
20	
21	`python3 document_room.py category policy.md --value "Legal Team"` assigns a single category to a registered document, and `DocumentRoom.set_category(relative_path, category)` does the same from Python; `--value` is required. The positional path matches the index's relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `archive`: it is never resolved against the filesystem, the file is not parsed, and the category can be changed even when the original file has been deleted. The category must be a string; it is stripped of leading and trailing whitespace and stored as a `category` field, preserving case and any inner whitespace, and the updated full record is printed as JSON with exit 0. An empty (or all-whitespace) value stores `""` and marks the document uncategorized. Records written before this feature simply lack the field and are treated as uncategorized, without the field being added. Setting a category changes nothing else: other metadata, references and the archived state are preserved.
22	
23	The first `add` of a path never stores a `category` field; re-adding a path that already has one keeps its category along with its references and archived state. `search` and `export` (CLI flag `--category`, Python argument `category`) accept an optional category filter: omitting it or passing `None` keeps the previous selection unchanged, while an explicit empty string selects only uncategorized records. Both the stored category and the filter value are stripped of surrounding whitespace and then compared as full case-sensitive strings, in conjunction with the existing tag, path-text and archive filters. Search still returns the complete stored records sorted by path; export keeps the same document fields, five file statuses and `complete` rule, and the category filter only chooses the starting documents — with `--with-references` every referenced document is pulled in recursively regardless of its category, with the usual dedup, cycle termination and `complete` rules.
24	
25	Setting a category, or filtering with a category other than `None`, validates the whole index: invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures, references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths, a non-boolean `archived` field, and a stored `category` that is not a string all raise `ValueError`, even when the bad record is not selected. A non-string category, a non-string or unregistered path, or a filter value that is neither a string nor `None` also raises `ValueError`; index read/write failures raise `OSError`, and failed input validation never changes the index. With no index, setting a category is treated as an unregistered path and creates no file, while filtering returns an empty result. The CLI prints JSON and exits 0 on success, or a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures.
26	
27	## Version notes
28	
29	`python3 document_room.py note policy.md --value "v2 draft"` attaches a free-form version note to a registered document, and `DocumentRoom.set_version_note(relative_path, note)` does the same from Python; `--value` is required. The positional path matches the index's relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `refs`: it is never resolved against the filesystem, the file is not parsed, and the note can be changed even when the original file has been deleted. The note must be a string; it is stripped of leading and trailing whitespace and stored as a `version_note` field, preserving case, inner whitespace and newlines, and the updated full record is printed as JSON with exit 0. An empty (or all-whitespace) value stores `""` and clears the note. Records written before this feature simply lack the field and are treated as having no note, without the field being added. Setting a note changes nothing else: other metadata, references, the archived state and the category are preserved.
30	
31	The first `add` of a path never stores a `version_note` field; re-adding a path that already has one keeps its note along with its references, archived state and category. `search` and `dump` return the stored note alongside the other metadata exactly as saved. `python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch" --with-version-notes` (or `export_manifest(..., include_version_notes=False)` with the flag on — the parameter is new, defaults to off, and the original parameter positions are unchanged) adds a `version_note` field to every manifest document: records without a stored note export `""`, and documents pulled in by reference expansion carry their own note. With the flag off no `version_note` field is added. Notes never participate in filtering, reference expansion, origin annotation, sorting, the five file statuses or the `complete` rule, and `compare` preserves the field in returned documents without comparing it.
32	
33	Setting a note, or exporting with notes enabled, validates the whole index: invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures or field types, references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths, and a stored `version_note` that is not a string all raise `ValueError`, even when the bad record is not selected. A non-string path or note, an unregistered path, or a non-boolean `include_version_notes` also raises `ValueError`; index read/write failures raise `OSError`, and failed input validation never changes the index. With no index, setting a note is treated as an unregistered path and creates no file, while a noted export returns an empty manifest with `complete` false. The CLI prints JSON and exits 0 on success, or a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures. Import keeps its existing conflict rules and extra-field preservation, and exporting never writes a manifest file or modifies the index or the original documents.
34	
35	## Release manifests
36	
37	`python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch" --tag legal --text policy` checks a release against the live files and prints `{"release", "complete", "documents"}`. The release name is required and trimmed; blank or non-string names raise `ValueError` from `DocumentRoom.export_manifest` (the CLI prints a JSON error and exits 2). `--tag` (repeatable, AND-combined) and `--text` (case-insensitive path substring) filter records with the same normalization as `search`. Documents are sorted by recorded relative path and keep their stored `path`, `name`, `bytes`, `sha256` and `tags`, plus a `status`:
38	
39	- `ready` — present, and both byte count and SHA-256 match the index;
40	- `changed` — present but the size or digest differs;
41	- `missing` — absent, a dangling symlink, or now a directory;
42	- `unsafe` — the resolved path escapes the document root (the target is never read);
43	- `unreadable` — any other resolution or read failure.
44	
45	Stored metadata is never overwritten with current values, and one document failing does not stop the others. `complete` is true only when the manifest is non-empty and every document is `ready`; an empty manifest still contains all three top-level fields. A missing index yields an empty manifest and is not created; malformed JSON or records whose structure/types do not match the registered format raise `ValueError`, and read failures raise `OSError`. Exporting only reads the index and files: it never copies documents, writes a manifest file or updates the index.
46	
47	## References
48	
49	`python3 document_room.py refs policy.md --to meeting.txt` records that a registered document directly refers to other registered documents, and `DocumentRoom.set_references(relative_path, targets)` does the same from Python. The source path is the positional argument and `--to` is repeatable; omitting `--to` clears the references. Paths match the index's relative-path keys exactly (case-sensitive) and are never resolved against the filesystem. Targets are deduplicated, sorted by path and stored as a `references` array on the record — an empty list is stored as `[]`. Self-references and mutual references are allowed. The updated record is returned as JSON and the CLI exits 0.
50	
51	A non-string source, an unregistered source or target, or targets that are not a list of strings raise `ValueError` without changing the index; a missing index is treated as empty and is not created. Corrupt JSON, records that do not match the registered format, a stored `references` field that is not a list of strings, or a stored reference to an unregistered path also raise `ValueError`, and index read/write failures raise `OSError`. Records written before this feature have no `references` field and are treated as having none: the first `add` of a path stores only the original fields, re-adding the same path keeps its references, and `search` returns any saved references alongside the other metadata.
52	
53	`python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch" --with-references` (or `export_manifest(..., include_references=True)`) expands the manifest: the usual tag and text filters pick the starting documents, then every referenced document is pulled in recursively — references are included whether or not they match the filters, each path appears once, and cycles still terminate. The manifest keeps the existing top-level and document fields sorted by path, every listed file is checked with the same status rules, and `complete` is false when any document is not `ready` or the manifest is empty. Reference-aware exports validate stored references as above; without the flag, export behaves exactly as before.
54	
55	## Reference origins
56	
57	`python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch" --with-references --with-origins` (or `export_manifest(..., include_references=True, include_origins=True)`) additionally records why each document entered the manifest. The option is off by default and requires reference expansion: a non-boolean `include_origins`, or enabling it without `include_references`, raises `ValueError`. Without the flag, export behaves exactly as before and no `origins` field is added.
58	
59	With origins enabled, every document gains an `origins` array whose entries are `{"path", "distance"}` objects: `path` is the registered path of a starting document (one selected by the tag, path-text, archive and category filters) and `distance` is the minimum number of reference edges from that starting document to this one, following the reference direction. Each reachable starting source appears at most once per document, a starting document lists itself with distance 0, shared documents keep every starting source, multiple routes collapse to the shortest distance, and self-references and cycles still terminate. `origins` is sorted by source path in case-sensitive lexicographic order, while `documents` keeps its usual path ordering. For example, with `a.md` and `b.md` selected, `a.md` referencing `c.md` directly and `b.md` reaching `c.md` through `d.md`, `c.md` lists `a.md` at distance 1 and `b.md` at distance 2 while `d.md` lists only `b.md`; if `c.md` also references `a.md`, then `a.md` additionally lists `b.md` at distance 3.
60	
61	Each document still appears once, an empty selection still yields an empty manifest with `complete` false, and the five file statuses and `complete` rule are unchanged. Enabling origins validates the whole index like reference expansion does — invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures or field types, and references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths raise `ValueError` even when the bad record is not selected, and index read failures raise `OSError`. Exporting remains read-only: it never writes a manifest file or updates the index, and a missing index is treated as empty without being created. `compare` preserves the `origins` field in returned documents like any other extra field and never compares it.
62	
63	## Reference impact
64	
65	`python3 document_room.py impact meeting.txt` answers the reverse question — which registered documents use a given document — and `DocumentRoom.reference_impact(target, transitive=False)` does the same from Python. The positional path identifies the target with the same exact, case-sensitive relative-path key as `refs`; it is never resolved against the filesystem. By default only direct referrers are returned; pass `--transitive` (or `transitive=True`) to also include every document that reaches the target through one or more reference edges. The command prints `{"path", "documents"}` and exits 0, where `path` echoes the input key.
66	
67	Each document is the same record `search` returns plus an integer `distance`: the minimum number of reference edges from that document to the target. Direct referrers always have distance 1; transitive results add documents at greater distances. Results are sorted by distance ascending and then by relative path lexicographically, each path appears once, and the target itself is always excluded even when it references itself. Self-references and reference cycles stay legal and the query always terminates. A registered target that nobody references yields an empty `documents` array.
68	
69	The impact query reads the stored index only: missing, changed or unreadable document files do not affect the result and no live file state is checked, and the index is never modified or created. A non-string or unregistered target, or a non-boolean `transitive`, raises `ValueError`; a missing index is treated as empty (so any target is unregistered and no file is created). Corrupt JSON, records that do not match the registered format, a `references` field that is not a list of strings, or a reference to an unregistered path also raises `ValueError` — even when the offending record is unrelated to the target — and index read failures raise `OSError`. The CLI reports these as a JSON object with an `error` field and exit code 2. Old records without a `references` field are treated as having none, and the field is not added.
70	
71	## Duplicate registration query
72	
73	`python3 document_room.py duplicates --tag release --text docs` finds registered documents whose stored contents coincide, and `DocumentRoom.find_duplicates(tags=(), text="")` does the same from Python; both paths give identical results. `--tag` is repeatable and `--text` takes one value, both filtered with the same normalization as `search` (tags are trimmed, lowercased, empty tags ignored and combined with AND; text matches the relative path case-insensitively). With no filter every record is considered.
74	
75	Two records are duplicates only when both stored `bytes` and stored `sha256` are equal — the digest is compared as the exact stored string — and a group needs at least two distinct paths. `name`, `tags` and `references` never participate in the judgement, so same-named records with different contents are not grouped. The result is `{"groups": []}` when there are no duplicates or no group has a member the filter matches.
76	
77	Each group is `{"bytes", "sha256", "matched", "documents"}`: `matched` lists the paths of members that satisfy the filter, `documents` lists the group's full stored records from the whole index (with whatever fields were stored, including `references` when present; neither `references` nor `status` is added). Both arrays are sorted by path and contain each path once, and the groups themselves are sorted by the smallest member path. A filter hitting any single member returns the entire group: querying the `release` tag when only `a.txt` of two identical small files (`a.txt`, `b.txt`) carries it still returns both records, with `matched` listing just `a.txt`.
78	
79	The query reads the stored index only: modifying, deleting or replacing an original file with an escaping symlink does not change the result or the index, and a missing index yields empty groups without creating a file. The Python `tags` argument must be a list or tuple of strings and `text` a string, otherwise `ValueError` is raised. Invalid JSON or UTF-8, records not matching the registered format, a `references` field that is not a list of strings, or a reference to an unregistered path also raise `ValueError` — even when the offending record is not in a returned group — and index read failures raise `OSError`. The CLI prints JSON and exits 0 on success, or an object with an `error` field and exit code 2 on failure.
80	
81	## Metadata import
82	
83	`python3 document_room.py import --from records.json` merges a batch of registrations from another index into the current one, and `DocumentRoom.import_records(batch)` does the same from Python with the decoded dictionary; both paths give identical results. The source is a UTF-8 JSON object mapping each relative-path key to a complete record whose `path` equals the key — the same shape as the stored index. Importing only copies metadata: document files are never read or copied, so records register fine while their files are missing.
84	
85	Records are stored exactly as given: paths, tags and categories are not normalized, optional fields (`references`, `archived`, `category`) are not added, and any extra JSON fields are preserved. A successful import returns `{"added", "unchanged"}` — the paths this batch newly registered and the input paths that already existed with identical records — each sorted by path in case-sensitive lexicographic order, and the CLI prints it as JSON and exits 0.
86	
87	A path already registered counts as unchanged only when the existing and incoming records have exactly the same field set and values: array order matters, object key order does not, and a missing optional field differs from its explicit default. A same-path record with different data fails the whole batch with `ValueError` and nothing is overwritten. Both the batch and the merged index are validated against the registered format — required field types, `bytes` as a non-boolean integer, and the optional `references`, `archived` and `category` types — so a malformed record fails the import even when its path is not part of the batch. Every reference target must be registered in the union of the existing index and the batch; forward references within the batch, self-references and cycles are allowed, and an unregistered target fails the whole batch with `ValueError`.
88	
89	A non-object batch, invalid structure or field types, a key that does not match its record's `path`, and corrupt JSON or UTF-8 in the source file raise `ValueError`; reading the source file or the index and writing the index raise `OSError`. Any failure leaves the source file and the existing index untouched and registers nothing. A missing index is treated as empty; an empty batch or a batch whose records are all identical to the stored ones neither writes nor creates the index. After an import, `search` returns the full stored records and `export` keeps its five statuses, origin annotation and `complete` rule.
90	
91	## Metadata snapshot export
92	
93	`python3 document_room.py dump --tag legal --text policy` prints a metadata snapshot of the selected records as a JSON object mapping each relative-path key to its complete stored record — the same shape `import` accepts — and `DocumentRoom.export_records(tags=(), text="", archive_state="all", category=None)` does the same from Python; both paths give identical results. The command uses the global `--root` and `--index` options, prints only the JSON object with no wrapper and no file statuses, and exits 0. The snapshot can be saved and merged into another (empty) index with `import --from`.
94	
95	`--tag` (repeatable, AND-combined), `--text` (case-insensitive path substring), `--archive-state` and `--category` filter with the same semantics as `search`, and with no filter every record is a starting document. The filters only choose the starting documents: every referenced document is then pulled in recursively along the reference direction regardless of the filters — archived or deleted files included — each path appears once, and self-references and cycles terminate. Documents that merely reference a selected one are not included. Records are returned exactly as stored: extra JSON fields are preserved, array order, duplicate elements, case and whitespace are untouched, and missing optional fields are not filled in. The object is keyed by path in case-sensitive lexicographic order.
96	
97	The whole index is validated before the result is returned: invalid JSON or UTF-8, records that do not match the registered format, and references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths raise `ValueError` even when the bad record is not selected. A `tags` argument that is not a list or tuple of strings, a non-string `text`, an illegal `archive_state`, or a `category` that is neither a string nor `None` also raises `ValueError`; index read failures raise `OSError`. The CLI reports these as a JSON object with an `error` field and exit code 2, printing no partial snapshot. A missing index or an empty selection yields an empty object and creates no file. Dumping is read-only: it never reads or copies the original documents, never writes a snapshot file, and never modifies the index.
98	
99	## Registration removal
100	
101	`python3 document_room.py remove meeting.txt` unregisters a single document's metadata record, and `DocumentRoom.remove_record(relative_path, detach=False)` does the same from Python. The positional path matches the index's relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `refs` and `archive`: it is never resolved against the filesystem, the document file is never read, moved or deleted, and removal works even when the original file has already been deleted. Only the index changes: no other registrations are recursively removed along reference edges.
102	
103	By default the operation is blocked with a `ValueError` whenever any *other* record's `references` contains the target path, and the index is left completely unchanged; the target's reference to itself never blocks its own removal. Records that merely reference one another transitively, without a direct edge to the target, do not block it. Pass `--detach` (or `detach=True`) to first remove every occurrence of the target from all other records' `references` and then remove the target's registration. Detaching preserves the order and any duplicate entries of the surviving references, never adds a `references` field to a record that lacked one, and stores `[]` on a record whose references all pointed at the target; every other field and every unaffected record keeps its stored value.
104	
105	A successful removal returns `{"removed", "updated"}`: `removed` is the target's complete record exactly as stored before the removal, and `updated` is an array of the complete records whose references were actually cleaned, sorted by path in case-sensitive lexicographic order — an empty array when nothing referenced the target (the default mode can only succeed in that case). The CLI prints the object as JSON and exits 0. After removal, `search`, `dump` and export operate on the remaining registrations; for example, once a referenced document is detached away, a reference-expanded listing only contains the surviving referrer.
106	
107	The whole index is validated against the same format `import` accepts before anything changes: a non-string or unregistered path, a non-boolean `detach`, corrupt JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures or field types, and references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths all raise `ValueError` even when the offending record is unrelated to the target, and failed validation never writes the index. Index read/write failures raise `OSError`. A missing index is treated as an empty room: removing any path is reported as unregistered and no file is created. The CLI prints a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures.
108	
109	## Manifest comparison
110	
111	`python3 document_room.py compare --before old.json --after new.json` diffs two manifests previously produced by `export` (plain UTF-8 JSON files), and `DocumentRoom.compare_manifests(before, after)` does the same from Python with the manifest dictionaries; both paths give identical results. The comparison relies solely on the manifest snapshots: the inputs and index are never modified, no document files are read, and nothing is created. The two manifests may use the same release name or different filter selections.
112	
113	The result is `{"before", "after", "added", "removed", "changed", "unchanged"}`. `before` and `after` echo each input's `release` and `complete` (release/complete differences never affect document classification and `complete` is never recomputed). `added` lists complete documents present only in the second manifest and `removed` those present only in the first; `changed` lists `{"path", "before", "after", "fields"}` keeping both full documents plus the changed field names; `unchanged` lists paths with no compared change.
114	
115	Documents pair by case-sensitive exact `path` (no normalization); only `name`, `bytes`, `sha256`, `tags` and `status` are compared. Tags compare as string sets, ignoring order and duplicates (but not case or whitespace); the other fields compare by value, so a `status`-only change still counts as changed. Extra document fields are preserved in the returned documents but never compared. Each category is sorted by path and `fields` is sorted by field name; each path appears exactly once. Two empty manifests yield four empty categories.
116	
117	Each input must be an object with a non-blank string `release`, a boolean `complete` and an array `documents`; every document needs string `path`, `name` and `sha256`, a non-boolean integer `bytes`, an array of strings `tags`, and one of the five statuses, with no duplicate paths within a manifest. Extra fields are allowed. Bad structure or types, duplicate paths, invalid statuses, and JSON or UTF-8 decode errors raise `ValueError` (the CLI prints a JSON error and exits 2); unreadable files raise `OSError`.
118	
119	Run `python3 -B -m unittest -v` for the API, path-boundary and CLI tests.

# Document Room

A local file metadata index. Python 3.10+ and the standard library are sufficient.

Run `python3 document_room.py add policy.md --tag legal --tag policy` from this directory to index the sample policy. Add the second sample with `python3 document_room.py add meeting.txt --tag operations`. `python3 document_room.py search --tag legal --text policy` returns matching metadata as JSON. Multiple tags are combined with AND; tags are trimmed and lowercase, and text matches the relative path without case sensitivity.

The default document root is `samples`; metadata is persisted in `.state/documents.json`. Override these with `--root` and `--index` before the subcommand. Re-adding a file refreshes its size, SHA-256 and tags. Search reads the stored metadata, not live file contents. Files must resolve inside the document root. This version does not copy documents, extract content or watch filesystem changes. Use the Python `DocumentRoom.add` and `DocumentRoom.search` methods for the same operations. CLI errors return JSON and exit 2.

## Document archiving

`python3 document_room.py archive meeting.txt` flips a registered document into the archived state without touching its file, and `DocumentRoom.set_archived(relative_path, archived)` does the same from Python; pass `--restore` (or `archived=False`) to mark it active again. The positional path matches the index's relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `refs`: it is never resolved against the filesystem, the file is not parsed, and archiving or restoring works even when the original file has been deleted. The state is stored as a boolean `archived` field on the record; records written before this feature simply lack the field and are treated as active, without the field being added. Restoring stores `archived: false` explicitly. Setting the same state twice returns the identical record, and no other metadata or references change. The updated full record is printed as JSON with exit 0.

The first `add` of a path never stores an `archived` field; re-adding a path that already has the field keeps its archived state along with its references. `search` and `export` (CLI flag `--archive-state`, Python argument `archive_state`) accept only `all`, `active` and `archived`; the default `all` keeps the previous selection unchanged. `active` selects records without a true `archived` field and `archived` only records with `archived: true`, in conjunction with the existing tag and path-text filters. Search still returns the complete stored records sorted by path without filling in a default field; export keeps the same document fields, five file statuses and `complete` rule.

With reference expansion (`export --with-references`), the archive filter only chooses the starting documents: every referenced document is pulled in recursively regardless of its archive state, each path still appears once and cycles still terminate. For example, an active `policy.md` that references an archived `meeting.txt` still produces a manifest containing both under `--archive-state active --with-references`.

Archiving only modifies the index; searching only reads stored metadata; exporting keeps its live file checks and never writes a manifest. Setting the archive state, or filtering with a state other than `all`, validates the whole index: invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures, references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths, and a non-boolean `archived` field all raise `ValueError`, even when the bad record is not selected. A non-string or unregistered path, a non-boolean `archived`, or a non-string/illegal `archive_state` also raises `ValueError`; index read/write failures raise `OSError`, and failed input validation never changes the index. With no index, setting the state is treated as an unregistered path and creates no file, while filtering returns an empty result (an empty manifest has `complete` false). The CLI prints JSON and exits 0 on success, or a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures.

## Document categories

`python3 document_room.py category policy.md --value "Legal Team"` assigns a single category to a registered document, and `DocumentRoom.set_category(relative_path, category)` does the same from Python; `--value` is required. The positional path matches the index's relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `archive`: it is never resolved against the filesystem, the file is not parsed, and the category can be changed even when the original file has been deleted. The category must be a string; it is stripped of leading and trailing whitespace and stored as a `category` field, preserving case and any inner whitespace, and the updated full record is printed as JSON with exit 0. An empty (or all-whitespace) value stores `""` and marks the document uncategorized. Records written before this feature simply lack the field and are treated as uncategorized, without the field being added. Setting a category changes nothing else: other metadata, references and the archived state are preserved.

The first `add` of a path never stores a `category` field; re-adding a path that already has one keeps its category along with its references and archived state. `search` and `export` (CLI flag `--category`, Python argument `category`) accept an optional category filter: omitting it or passing `None` keeps the previous selection unchanged, while an explicit empty string selects only uncategorized records. Both the stored category and the filter value are stripped of surrounding whitespace and then compared as full case-sensitive strings, in conjunction with the existing tag, path-text and archive filters. Search still returns the complete stored records sorted by path; export keeps the same document fields, five file statuses and `complete` rule, and the category filter only chooses the starting documents — with `--with-references` every referenced document is pulled in recursively regardless of its category, with the usual dedup, cycle termination and `complete` rules.

Setting a category, or filtering with a category other than `None`, validates the whole index: invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures, references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths, a non-boolean `archived` field, and a stored `category` that is not a string all raise `ValueError`, even when the bad record is not selected. A non-string category, a non-string or unregistered path, or a filter value that is neither a string nor `None` also raises `ValueError`; index read/write failures raise `OSError`, and failed input validation never changes the index. With no index, setting a category is treated as an unregistered path and creates no file, while filtering returns an empty result. The CLI prints JSON and exits 0 on success, or a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures.

## Version notes

`python3 document_room.py note policy.md --value "v2 draft"` attaches a free-form version note to a registered document, and `DocumentRoom.set_version_note(relative_path, note)` does the same from Python; `--value` is required. The positional path matches the index's relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `refs`: it is never resolved against the filesystem, the file is not parsed, and the note can be changed even when the original file has been deleted. The note must be a string; it is stripped of leading and trailing whitespace and stored as a `version_note` field, preserving case, inner whitespace and newlines, and the updated full record is printed as JSON with exit 0. An empty (or all-whitespace) value stores `""` and clears the note. Records written before this feature simply lack the field and are treated as having no note, without the field being added. Setting a note changes nothing else: other metadata, references, the archived state and the category are preserved.

The first `add` of a path never stores a `version_note` field; re-adding a path that already has one keeps its note along with its references, archived state and category. `search` and `dump` return the stored note alongside the other metadata exactly as saved. `python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch" --with-version-notes` (or `export_manifest(..., include_version_notes=False)` with the flag on — the parameter is new, defaults to off, and the original parameter positions are unchanged) adds a `version_note` field to every manifest document: records without a stored note export `""`, and documents pulled in by reference expansion carry their own note. With the flag off no `version_note` field is added. Notes never participate in filtering, reference expansion, origin annotation, sorting, the five file statuses or the `complete` rule, and `compare` preserves the field in returned documents without comparing it.

Setting a note, or exporting with notes enabled, validates the whole index: invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures or field types, references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths, and a stored `version_note` that is not a string all raise `ValueError`, even when the bad record is not selected. A non-string path or note, an unregistered path, or a non-boolean `include_version_notes` also raises `ValueError`; index read/write failures raise `OSError`, and failed input validation never changes the index. With no index, setting a note is treated as an unregistered path and creates no file, while a noted export returns an empty manifest with `complete` false. The CLI prints JSON and exits 0 on success, or a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures. Import keeps its existing conflict rules and extra-field preservation, and exporting never writes a manifest file or modifies the index or the original documents.

## Release manifests

`python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch" --tag legal --text policy` checks a release against the live files and prints `{"release", "complete", "documents"}`. The release name is required and trimmed; blank or non-string names raise `ValueError` from `DocumentRoom.export_manifest` (the CLI prints a JSON error and exits 2). `--tag` (repeatable, AND-combined) and `--text` (case-insensitive path substring) filter records with the same normalization as `search`. Documents are sorted by recorded relative path and keep their stored `path`, `name`, `bytes`, `sha256` and `tags`, plus a `status`:

- `ready` — present, and both byte count and SHA-256 match the index;
- `changed` — present but the size or digest differs;
- `missing` — absent, a dangling symlink, or now a directory;
- `unsafe` — the resolved path escapes the document root (the target is never read);
- `unreadable` — any other resolution or read failure.

Stored metadata is never overwritten with current values, and one document failing does not stop the others. `complete` is true only when the manifest is non-empty and every document is `ready`; an empty manifest still contains all three top-level fields. A missing index yields an empty manifest and is not created; malformed JSON or records whose structure/types do not match the registered format raise `ValueError`, and read failures raise `OSError`. Exporting only reads the index and files: it never copies documents, writes a manifest file or updates the index.

## References

`python3 document_room.py refs policy.md --to meeting.txt` records that a registered document directly refers to other registered documents, and `DocumentRoom.set_references(relative_path, targets)` does the same from Python. The source path is the positional argument and `--to` is repeatable; omitting `--to` clears the references. Paths match the index's relative-path keys exactly (case-sensitive) and are never resolved against the filesystem. Targets are deduplicated, sorted by path and stored as a `references` array on the record — an empty list is stored as `[]`. Self-references and mutual references are allowed. The updated record is returned as JSON and the CLI exits 0.

A non-string source, an unregistered source or target, or targets that are not a list of strings raise `ValueError` without changing the index; a missing index is treated as empty and is not created. Corrupt JSON, records that do not match the registered format, a stored `references` field that is not a list of strings, or a stored reference to an unregistered path also raise `ValueError`, and index read/write failures raise `OSError`. Records written before this feature have no `references` field and are treated as having none: the first `add` of a path stores only the original fields, re-adding the same path keeps its references, and `search` returns any saved references alongside the other metadata.

`python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch" --with-references` (or `export_manifest(..., include_references=True)`) expands the manifest: the usual tag and text filters pick the starting documents, then every referenced document is pulled in recursively — references are included whether or not they match the filters, each path appears once, and cycles still terminate. The manifest keeps the existing top-level and document fields sorted by path, every listed file is checked with the same status rules, and `complete` is false when any document is not `ready` or the manifest is empty. Reference-aware exports validate stored references as above; without the flag, export behaves exactly as before.

## Reference origins

`python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch" --with-references --with-origins` (or `export_manifest(..., include_references=True, include_origins=True)`) additionally records why each document entered the manifest. The option is off by default and requires reference expansion: a non-boolean `include_origins`, or enabling it without `include_references`, raises `ValueError`. Without the flag, export behaves exactly as before and no `origins` field is added.

With origins enabled, every document gains an `origins` array whose entries are `{"path", "distance"}` objects: `path` is the registered path of a starting document (one selected by the tag, path-text, archive and category filters) and `distance` is the minimum number of reference edges from that starting document to this one, following the reference direction. Each reachable starting source appears at most once per document, a starting document lists itself with distance 0, shared documents keep every starting source, multiple routes collapse to the shortest distance, and self-references and cycles still terminate. `origins` is sorted by source path in case-sensitive lexicographic order, while `documents` keeps its usual path ordering. For example, with `a.md` and `b.md` selected, `a.md` referencing `c.md` directly and `b.md` reaching `c.md` through `d.md`, `c.md` lists `a.md` at distance 1 and `b.md` at distance 2 while `d.md` lists only `b.md`; if `c.md` also references `a.md`, then `a.md` additionally lists `b.md` at distance 3.

Each document still appears once, an empty selection still yields an empty manifest with `complete` false, and the five file statuses and `complete` rule are unchanged. Enabling origins validates the whole index like reference expansion does — invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures or field types, and references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths raise `ValueError` even when the bad record is not selected, and index read failures raise `OSError`. Exporting remains read-only: it never writes a manifest file or updates the index, and a missing index is treated as empty without being created. `compare` preserves the `origins` field in returned documents like any other extra field and never compares it.

## Reference impact

`python3 document_room.py impact meeting.txt` answers the reverse question — which registered documents use a given document — and `DocumentRoom.reference_impact(target, transitive=False)` does the same from Python. The positional path identifies the target with the same exact, case-sensitive relative-path key as `refs`; it is never resolved against the filesystem. By default only direct referrers are returned; pass `--transitive` (or `transitive=True`) to also include every document that reaches the target through one or more reference edges. The command prints `{"path", "documents"}` and exits 0, where `path` echoes the input key.

Each document is the same record `search` returns plus an integer `distance`: the minimum number of reference edges from that document to the target. Direct referrers always have distance 1; transitive results add documents at greater distances. Results are sorted by distance ascending and then by relative path lexicographically, each path appears once, and the target itself is always excluded even when it references itself. Self-references and reference cycles stay legal and the query always terminates. A registered target that nobody references yields an empty `documents` array.

The impact query reads the stored index only: missing, changed or unreadable document files do not affect the result and no live file state is checked, and the index is never modified or created. A non-string or unregistered target, or a non-boolean `transitive`, raises `ValueError`; a missing index is treated as empty (so any target is unregistered and no file is created). Corrupt JSON, records that do not match the registered format, a `references` field that is not a list of strings, or a reference to an unregistered path also raises `ValueError` — even when the offending record is unrelated to the target — and index read failures raise `OSError`. The CLI reports these as a JSON object with an `error` field and exit code 2. Old records without a `references` field are treated as having none, and the field is not added.

## Duplicate registration query

`python3 document_room.py duplicates --tag release --text docs` finds registered documents whose stored contents coincide, and `DocumentRoom.find_duplicates(tags=(), text="")` does the same from Python; both paths give identical results. `--tag` is repeatable and `--text` takes one value, both filtered with the same normalization as `search` (tags are trimmed, lowercased, empty tags ignored and combined with AND; text matches the relative path case-insensitively). With no filter every record is considered.

Two records are duplicates only when both stored `bytes` and stored `sha256` are equal — the digest is compared as the exact stored string — and a group needs at least two distinct paths. `name`, `tags` and `references` never participate in the judgement, so same-named records with different contents are not grouped. The result is `{"groups": []}` when there are no duplicates or no group has a member the filter matches.

Each group is `{"bytes", "sha256", "matched", "documents"}`: `matched` lists the paths of members that satisfy the filter, `documents` lists the group's full stored records from the whole index (with whatever fields were stored, including `references` when present; neither `references` nor `status` is added). Both arrays are sorted by path and contain each path once, and the groups themselves are sorted by the smallest member path. A filter hitting any single member returns the entire group: querying the `release` tag when only `a.txt` of two identical small files (`a.txt`, `b.txt`) carries it still returns both records, with `matched` listing just `a.txt`.

The query reads the stored index only: modifying, deleting or replacing an original file with an escaping symlink does not change the result or the index, and a missing index yields empty groups without creating a file. The Python `tags` argument must be a list or tuple of strings and `text` a string, otherwise `ValueError` is raised. Invalid JSON or UTF-8, records not matching the registered format, a `references` field that is not a list of strings, or a reference to an unregistered path also raise `ValueError` — even when the offending record is not in a returned group — and index read failures raise `OSError`. The CLI prints JSON and exits 0 on success, or an object with an `error` field and exit code 2 on failure.

## Metadata import

`python3 document_room.py import --from records.json` merges a batch of registrations from another index into the current one, and `DocumentRoom.import_records(batch)` does the same from Python with the decoded dictionary; both paths give identical results. The source is a UTF-8 JSON object mapping each relative-path key to a complete record whose `path` equals the key — the same shape as the stored index. Importing only copies metadata: document files are never read or copied, so records register fine while their files are missing.

Records are stored exactly as given: paths, tags and categories are not normalized, optional fields (`references`, `archived`, `category`) are not added, and any extra JSON fields are preserved. A successful import returns `{"added", "unchanged"}` — the paths this batch newly registered and the input paths that already existed with identical records — each sorted by path in case-sensitive lexicographic order, and the CLI prints it as JSON and exits 0.

A path already registered counts as unchanged only when the existing and incoming records have exactly the same field set and values: array order matters, object key order does not, and a missing optional field differs from its explicit default. A same-path record with different data fails the whole batch with `ValueError` and nothing is overwritten. Both the batch and the merged index are validated against the registered format — required field types, `bytes` as a non-boolean integer, and the optional `references`, `archived` and `category` types — so a malformed record fails the import even when its path is not part of the batch. Every reference target must be registered in the union of the existing index and the batch; forward references within the batch, self-references and cycles are allowed, and an unregistered target fails the whole batch with `ValueError`.

A non-object batch, invalid structure or field types, a key that does not match its record's `path`, and corrupt JSON or UTF-8 in the source file raise `ValueError`; reading the source file or the index and writing the index raise `OSError`. Any failure leaves the source file and the existing index untouched and registers nothing. A missing index is treated as empty; an empty batch or a batch whose records are all identical to the stored ones neither writes nor creates the index. After an import, `search` returns the full stored records and `export` keeps its five statuses, origin annotation and `complete` rule.

## Metadata snapshot export

`python3 document_room.py dump --tag legal --text policy` prints a metadata snapshot of the selected records as a JSON object mapping each relative-path key to its complete stored record — the same shape `import` accepts — and `DocumentRoom.export_records(tags=(), text="", archive_state="all", category=None)` does the same from Python; both paths give identical results. The command uses the global `--root` and `--index` options, prints only the JSON object with no wrapper and no file statuses, and exits 0. The snapshot can be saved and merged into another (empty) index with `import --from`.

`--tag` (repeatable, AND-combined), `--text` (case-insensitive path substring), `--archive-state` and `--category` filter with the same semantics as `search`, and with no filter every record is a starting document. The filters only choose the starting documents: every referenced document is then pulled in recursively along the reference direction regardless of the filters — archived or deleted files included — each path appears once, and self-references and cycles terminate. Documents that merely reference a selected one are not included. Records are returned exactly as stored: extra JSON fields are preserved, array order, duplicate elements, case and whitespace are untouched, and missing optional fields are not filled in. The object is keyed by path in case-sensitive lexicographic order.

The whole index is validated before the result is returned: invalid JSON or UTF-8, records that do not match the registered format, and references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths raise `ValueError` even when the bad record is not selected. A `tags` argument that is not a list or tuple of strings, a non-string `text`, an illegal `archive_state`, or a `category` that is neither a string nor `None` also raises `ValueError`; index read failures raise `OSError`. The CLI reports these as a JSON object with an `error` field and exit code 2, printing no partial snapshot. A missing index or an empty selection yields an empty object and creates no file. Dumping is read-only: it never reads or copies the original documents, never writes a snapshot file, and never modifies the index.

## Registration removal

`python3 document_room.py remove meeting.txt` unregisters a single document's metadata record, and `DocumentRoom.remove_record(relative_path, detach=False)` does the same from Python. The positional path matches the index's relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `refs` and `archive`: it is never resolved against the filesystem, the document file is never read, moved or deleted, and removal works even when the original file has already been deleted. Only the index changes: no other registrations are recursively removed along reference edges.

By default the operation is blocked with a `ValueError` whenever any *other* record's `references` contains the target path, and the index is left completely unchanged; the target's reference to itself never blocks its own removal. Records that merely reference one another transitively, without a direct edge to the target, do not block it. Pass `--detach` (or `detach=True`) to first remove every occurrence of the target from all other records' `references` and then remove the target's registration. Detaching preserves the order and any duplicate entries of the surviving references, never adds a `references` field to a record that lacked one, and stores `[]` on a record whose references all pointed at the target; every other field and every unaffected record keeps its stored value.

A successful removal returns `{"removed", "updated"}`: `removed` is the target's complete record exactly as stored before the removal, and `updated` is an array of the complete records whose references were actually cleaned, sorted by path in case-sensitive lexicographic order — an empty array when nothing referenced the target (the default mode can only succeed in that case). The CLI prints the object as JSON and exits 0. After removal, `search`, `dump` and export operate on the remaining registrations; for example, once a referenced document is detached away, a reference-expanded listing only contains the surviving referrer.

The whole index is validated against the same format `import` accepts before anything changes: a non-string or unregistered path, a non-boolean `detach`, corrupt JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures or field types, and references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths all raise `ValueError` even when the offending record is unrelated to the target, and failed validation never writes the index. Index read/write failures raise `OSError`. A missing index is treated as an empty room: removing any path is reported as unregistered and no file is created. The CLI prints a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures.

## Manifest comparison

`python3 document_room.py compare --before old.json --after new.json` diffs two manifests previously produced by `export` (plain UTF-8 JSON files), and `DocumentRoom.compare_manifests(before, after)` does the same from Python with the manifest dictionaries; both paths give identical results. The comparison relies solely on the manifest snapshots: the inputs and index are never modified, no document files are read, and nothing is created. The two manifests may use the same release name or different filter selections.

The result is `{"before", "after", "added", "removed", "changed", "unchanged"}`. `before` and `after` echo each input's `release` and `complete` (release/complete differences never affect document classification and `complete` is never recomputed). `added` lists complete documents present only in the second manifest and `removed` those present only in the first; `changed` lists `{"path", "before", "after", "fields"}` keeping both full documents plus the changed field names; `unchanged` lists paths with no compared change.

Documents pair by case-sensitive exact `path` (no normalization); only `name`, `bytes`, `sha256`, `tags` and `status` are compared. Tags compare as string sets, ignoring order and duplicates (but not case or whitespace); the other fields compare by value, so a `status`-only change still counts as changed. Extra document fields are preserved in the returned documents but never compared. Each category is sorted by path and `fields` is sorted by field name; each path appears exactly once. Two empty manifests yield four empty categories.

Each input must be an object with a non-blank string `release`, a boolean `complete` and an array `documents`; every document needs string `path`, `name` and `sha256`, a non-boolean integer `bytes`, an array of strings `tags`, and one of the five statuses, with no duplicate paths within a manifest. Extra fields are allowed. Bad structure or types, duplicate paths, invalid statuses, and JSON or UTF-8 decode errors raise `ValueError` (the CLI prints a JSON error and exits 2); unreadable files raise `OSError`.

Run `python3 -B -m unittest -v` for the API, path-boundary and CLI tests.

199	        for key, record in records.items():

209	                raise ValueError("record has invalid field types")
210	            if "archived" in record and not isinstance(record["archived"], bool):
211	                raise ValueError("record archived must be a boolean")
212	            references = record.get("references", [])

219	    def import_records(self, batch):
220	        if not isinstance(batch, dict):
221	            raise ValueError("import batch must be an object of records")
222	        existing = self._load()
223	        if not isinstance(existing, dict):
224	            raise ValueError("index must be a JSON object of records")
225	        # Bad records fail the whole batch even when their paths are not imported.
226	        self._validate_importable(existing)
227	        self._validate_importable(batch)
228	        added = []
229	        unchanged = []
230	        for key, record in batch.items():
231	            if key not in existing:
232	                added.append(key)
233	            elif existing[key] == record:  # field set and values, arrays ordered
234	                unchanged.append(key)
235	            else:
236	                raise ValueError("import conflicts with the existing record: " + key)
237	        merged = dict(existing)
238	        for key in added:
239	            merged[key] = batch[key]
240	        for record in merged.values():
241	            for target in record.get("references", []):
242	                if target not in merged:
243	                    raise ValueError("record references an unregistered path")
244	        if added:
245	            self.index.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
246	            self.index.write_text(json.dumps(merged, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
247	                                  encoding="utf-8")
248	        return {"added": sorted(added), "unchanged": sorted(unchanged)}

250	    def export_records(self, tags=(), text="", archive_state="all", category=None):
251	        if not isinstance(tags, (list, tuple)) or not all(isinstance(tag, str) for tag in tags):
252	            raise ValueError("tags must be a list or tuple of strings")
253	        if not isinstance(text, str):
254	            raise ValueError("text must be a string")
255	        self._check_archive_state(archive_state)
256	        self._check_category_filter(category)
257	        records = self._load_validated_with_categories()
258	        wanted = {tag.strip().lower() for tag in tags if tag.strip()}
259	
260	        def matches(record):
261	            return (wanted.issubset(record["tags"])
262	                    and text.casefold() in record["path"].casefold()
263	                    and self._matches_archive_state(record, archive_state)
264	                    and self._matches_category(record, category))
265	
266	        selected = {}
267	        stack = [key for key, record in records.items() if matches(record)]
268	        while stack:
269	            key = stack.pop()
270	            if key in selected:
271	                continue
272	            selected[key] = records[key]
273	            # Dependencies are pulled in regardless of the filters; records
274	            # that merely reference a selected one are not.
275	            stack.extend(records[key].get("references", []))
276	        return {key: selected[key] for key in sorted(selected)}

278	    def reference_impact(self, target, transitive=False):
279	        if not isinstance(target, str):
280	            raise ValueError("target path must be a string")
281	        if not isinstance(transitive, bool):
282	            raise ValueError("transitive must be a boolean")
283	        records = self._load_validated_with_references()
284	        if target not in records:
285	            raise ValueError("target document is not registered")
286	        referrers = {}
287	        for source, record in records.items():
288	            for referenced in record.get("references", []):
289	                referrers.setdefault(referenced, set()).add(source)
290	        distances = {}
291	        frontier = [target]
292	        depth = 0
293	        while frontier and (transitive or depth == 0):
294	            nxt = []
295	            for node in frontier:
296	                for source in referrers.get(node, ()):  # reverse reference edges
297	                    if source != target and source not in distances:
298	                        distances[source] = depth + 1
299	                        nxt.append(source)
300	            frontier = nxt
301	            depth += 1
302	        documents = [{**records[key], "distance": distances[key]}
303	                     for key in sorted(distances, key=lambda key: (distances[key], key))]
304	        return {"path": target, "documents": documents}

306	    def search(self, tags=(), text="", archive_state="all", category=None):
307	        self._check_archive_state(archive_state)

309	        wanted = {tag.strip().lower() for tag in tags if tag.strip()}
310	        if archive_state == "all" and category is None:
311	            records = self._load()
312	        else:  # a non-trivial filter validates the whole index, references included
313	            records = self._load_validated_with_categories()
314	        return [record for _, record in sorted(records.items())
315	                if wanted.issubset(record["tags"])
316	                and text.casefold() in record["path"].casefold()
317	                and self._matches_archive_state(record, archive_state)
318	                and self._matches_category(record, category)]

320	    def find_duplicates(self, tags=(), text=""):
321	        if not isinstance(tags, (list, tuple)) or not all(isinstance(tag, str) for tag in tags):
322	            raise ValueError("tags must be a list or tuple of strings")
323	        if not isinstance(text, str):
324	            raise ValueError("text must be a string")
325	        records = self._load_validated_with_references()
326	        wanted = {tag.strip().lower() for tag in tags if tag.strip()}
327	
328	        def matches(record):
329	            return (wanted.issubset(record["tags"])
330	                    and text.casefold() in record["path"].casefold())
331	
332	        buckets = {}
333	        for record in records.values():
334	            buckets.setdefault((record["bytes"], record["sha256"]), []).append(record)
335	        groups = []
336	        for (size, digest), members in buckets.items():
337	            if len(members) < 2:  # duplicates need at least two distinct paths
338	                continue
339	            paths = sorted(record["path"] for record in members)
340	            matched = [path for path in paths if matches(records[path])]
341	            if not matched:  # a filter must hit at least one member to return the group
342	                continue
343	            groups.append({"bytes": size, "sha256": digest, "matched": matched,
344	                           "documents": [records[path] for path in paths]})
345	        groups.sort(key=lambda group: group["documents"][0]["path"])
346	        return {"groups": groups}

348	    def _file_status(self, record):
349	        try:
350	            path = (self.root / record["path"]).resolve()
351	            if not path.is_relative_to(self.root):
352	                return "unsafe"
353	            if not path.is_file():
354	                return "missing"
355	            content = path.read_bytes()
356	            return ("ready" if len(content) == record["bytes"]
357	                    and hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest() == record["sha256"]
358	                    else "changed")
359	        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError):
360	            return "unreadable"

362	    def export_manifest(self, release, tags=(), text="", include_references=False,
363	                        archive_state="all", category=None, include_origins=False,
364	                        include_version_notes=False):
365	        if not isinstance(release, str) or not release.strip():
366	            raise ValueError("release must be a non-empty string")
367	        self._check_archive_state(archive_state)
368	        self._check_category_filter(category)
369	        if not isinstance(include_origins, bool):
370	            raise ValueError("include_origins must be a boolean")
371	        if include_origins and not include_references:
372	            raise ValueError("include_origins requires include_references")
373	        if not isinstance(include_version_notes, bool):
374	            raise ValueError("include_version_notes must be a boolean")
375	        release = release.strip()
376	        wanted = {tag.strip().lower() for tag in tags if tag.strip()}
377	
378	        def matches(record):
379	            return (wanted.issubset(record["tags"])
380	                    and text.casefold() in record["path"].casefold()
381	                    and self._matches_archive_state(record, archive_state)
382	                    and self._matches_category(record, category))
383	
384	        if include_version_notes:
385	            records = self._load_validated_with_version_notes()
386	        elif include_references or archive_state != "all" or category is not None:
387	            records = self._load_validated_with_categories()
388	        else:
389	            records = self._load_validated()
390	        if include_references:
391	            selected = {}
392	            starts = [key for key, record in records.items() if matches(record)]
393	            stack = list(starts)
394	            while stack:
395	                key = stack.pop()
396	                if key in selected:
397	                    continue
398	                selected[key] = records[key]
399	                # Referenced documents are pulled in regardless of archive state
400	                # or category.
401	                stack.extend(records[key].get("references", []))
402	            ordered = [selected[key] for key in sorted(selected)]
403	            origins = {}
404	            if include_origins:
405	                # Breadth-first from each starting document along the reference
406	                # direction; every reachable document keeps the shortest distance
407	                # per starting source.
408	                for start in starts:
409	                    distances = {start: 0}
410	                    frontier = [start]
411	                    depth = 0
412	                    while frontier:
413	                        nxt = []
414	                        for node in frontier:
415	                            for target in records[node].get("references", []):
416	                                if target not in distances:
417	                                    distances[target] = depth + 1
418	                                    nxt.append(target)
419	                        frontier = nxt
420	                        depth += 1
421	                    for key, distance in distances.items():
422	                        per_document = origins.setdefault(key, {})
423	                        if start not in per_document or distance < per_document[start]:
424	                            per_document[start] = distance
425	        else:
426	            ordered = [record for _, record in sorted(records.items()) if matches(record)]
427	        documents = []
428	        for record in ordered:
429	            document = {"path": record["path"], "name": record["name"],
430	                        "bytes": record["bytes"], "sha256": record["sha256"],
431	                        "tags": record["tags"], "status": self._file_status(record)}
432	            if include_origins:
433	                document["origins"] = [
434	                    {"path": source, "distance": origins[record["path"]][source]}
435	                    for source in sorted(origins[record["path"]])]
436	            if include_version_notes:
437	                # Records written before this feature lack the field and
438	                # export an empty note; referenced documents keep their own.
439	                document["version_note"] = record.get("version_note", "")
440	            documents.append(document)
441	        return {"release": release,
442	                "complete": bool(documents) and all(d["status"] == "ready" for d in documents),
443	                "documents": documents}

445	    @staticmethod
446	    def _validated_manifest(manifest):
447	        if not isinstance(manifest, dict):
448	            raise ValueError("manifest must be a JSON object")
449	        release = manifest.get("release")
450	        if not isinstance(release, str) or not release.strip():
451	            raise ValueError("manifest release must be a non-blank string")
452	        if not isinstance(manifest.get("complete"), bool):
453	            raise ValueError("manifest complete must be a boolean")
454	        documents = manifest.get("documents")
455	        if not isinstance(documents, list):
456	            raise ValueError("manifest documents must be an array")
457	        seen = set()
458	        for document in documents:
459	            if not isinstance(document, dict):
460	                raise ValueError("manifest document must be an object")
461	            path = document.get("path")
462	            if not isinstance(path, str):
463	                raise ValueError("manifest document path must be a string")
464	            if path in seen:
465	                raise ValueError("manifest contains a duplicate path")
466	            seen.add(path)
467	            if not isinstance(document.get("name"), str):
468	                raise ValueError("manifest document name must be a string")
469	            if not isinstance(document.get("sha256"), str):
470	                raise ValueError("manifest document sha256 must be a string")
471	            if (not isinstance(document.get("bytes"), int)
472	                    or isinstance(document.get("bytes"), bool)):
473	                raise ValueError("manifest document bytes must be a non-boolean integer")
474	            tags = document.get("tags")
475	            if not isinstance(tags, list) or not all(isinstance(tag, str) for tag in tags):
476	                raise ValueError("manifest document tags must be an array of strings")
477	            if document.get("status") not in DocumentRoom.STATUSES:
478	                raise ValueError("manifest document status must be one of "
479	                                 + ", ".join(sorted(DocumentRoom.STATUSES)))
480	        return manifest

482	    @staticmethod
483	    def compare_manifests(before, after):
484	        before = DocumentRoom._validated_manifest(before)
485	        after = DocumentRoom._validated_manifest(after)
486	        before_docs = {d["path"]: d for d in before["documents"]}
487	        after_docs = {d["path"]: d for d in after["documents"]}
488	        before_paths = set(before_docs)
489	        after_paths = set(after_docs)
490	        changed = []
491	        unchanged = []
492	        for path in sorted(before_paths & after_paths):
493	            old = before_docs[path]
494	            new = after_docs[path]
495	            fields = []
496	            for field in DocumentRoom.COMPARED_FIELDS:
497	                if field == "tags":
498	                    differs = set(old["tags"]) != set(new["tags"])
499	                else:
500	                    differs = old[field] != new[field]
501	                if differs:
502	                    fields.append(field)
503	            if fields:
504	                changed.append({"path": path, "before": old, "after": new,
505	                                "fields": fields})
506	            else:
507	                unchanged.append(path)
508	        return {
509	            "before": {"release": before["release"], "complete": before["complete"]},
510	            "after": {"release": after["release"], "complete": after["complete"]},
511	            "added": [after_docs[path] for path in sorted(after_paths - before_paths)],
512	            "removed": [before_docs[path] for path in sorted(before_paths - after_paths)],
513	            "changed": changed,
514	            "unchanged": unchanged,
515	        }
516	
517	    @staticmethod
518	    def compare_manifest_files(before_path, after_path):
519	        def load(path):
520	            with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
521	                return json.load(handle)
522	        try:
523	            before = load(before_path)
524	            after = load(after_path)
525	        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
526	            raise ValueError(f"manifest file is not valid UTF-8: {exc}")
527	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
528	            raise ValueError(f"manifest file is not valid JSON: {exc}")
529	        return DocumentRoom.compare_manifests(before, after)

Install
python3 --version
Python 3.10 or newer; no third-party dependencies.

Start
python3 document_room.py add policy.md --tag legal --tag policy
Prints metadata for the sample policy and saves the local index.

Smoke Test
python3 document_room.py search --tag legal
Returns the policy metadata in a JSON array.
python3 document_room.py archive meeting.txt
Marks a registered document archived (index only; --restore marks it active); search/export accept --archive-state all|active|archived, defaulting to all.
python3 document_room.py category policy.md --value "Legal Team"
Assigns a single category to a registered document (index only; an empty value marks it uncategorized); search/export accept --category to filter, and omitting it keeps every category.
python3 document_room.py note policy.md --value "v2 draft"
Attaches a free-form version note to a registered document (index only; a blank value clears it); export --with-version-notes adds each document's note to the manifest.
python3 document_room.py remove meeting.txt --detach
Unregisters one document's metadata record by exact index key (index only; the file is never touched); default mode is blocked while another record references it, and --detach clears those references first.
python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch"
Checks the registered files and reports ready, changed, missing, unsafe or unreadable; complete is true only when every listed document is ready.
python3 document_room.py impact meeting.txt
Lists registered documents that reference the target, each with its minimum reference-edge distance; --transitive also includes indirect referrers.
python3 document_room.py duplicates --tag release
Groups registrations with equal stored bytes and SHA-256 into duplicate groups; --tag (repeatable) and --text filter like search and any member match returns the whole group.
python3 document_room.py compare --before old.json --after new.json
Diffs two exported manifest snapshots into added, removed, changed and unchanged documents without touching the index or files.
python3 document_room.py import --from records.json
Merges a UTF-8 JSON object of path-keyed records into the index (metadata only; files are not read), reporting added and unchanged paths; conflicting or invalid records fail the whole batch with exit 2.
python3 -B -m unittest -v
